bib.title: 5 Pretraining on unlabeled data (Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch))
bib.venue: book chapter (Manning); author and year not printed in the extracted text (author per ledger/note citation: Raschka, 2024)

question: How do you evaluate generated text with a loss, pretrain a small GPT on unlabeled text, control decoding randomness, save/load weights, and load OpenAI's GPT-2 weights?
contributions: Cross-entropy loss and perplexity as the text-quality measure
Temperature scaling and top-k sampling in a generate function
Loading OpenAI GPT-2 weights (124M to 1558M) into GPTModel

results.claim: With a toy logit vector and 1,000 multinomial draws, 'forward' is sampled 582 times (the most likely token), 'toward' 343, 'closer' 73, 'inches' 2.
results.quote:
the word forward is sampled most of the time (582 out of
1,000 times)

results.claim: At temperature 5, 'pizza' is sampled about 4% of the time in the toy example.
results.quote:
every effort
moves you pizza about 4% of the time

results.claim: Top-k with k=3 on the toy logits gives probabilities 0.0615, 0.5775, 0.3610 for the three kept tokens.
OpenAI GPT-2 124M checkpoint data file is 498M; seven files are downloaded; settings are n_vocab 50257, n_ctx 1024, n_embd 768, n_head 12, n_layer 12.
Loading OpenAI GPT-2 124M into GPTModel needs context_length 1024 and qkv_bias True; text generated with top_k=50, temperature=1.5 is coherent.
results.setup: GPT-2 small via NEW_CONFIG, seed 123, 25 new tokens

limits: Toy scale: 5,145 tokens, batch size 2, 10 epochs; the author says real LLM pretraining uses far larger data and typically one epoch.
Final validation loss 6.452 vs train 0.391: the trained model overfits and memorises; no held-out quality metric beyond loss.
Loss and perplexity computed on tiny samples; no benchmark evaluation.
Single run with seed 123; no variance reported.
Training loop omits learning-rate warmup, cosine decay and gradient clipping (deferred to an appendix).
Chapter cross-references the larger Gutenberg run inconsistently (appendix D at 5.1.3, appendix B at 5.2).
Llama 2 cost figures are uncited and rough.
Weight loading depends on OpenAI's TensorFlow checkpoint format and a download script that may change.
practices: Compute training and validation cross-entropy over the whole loader and track both during training (5.1.3, 5.2).
Use model.eval() and torch.no_grad() when evaluating or generating (5.2).
Use AdamW (decoupled weight decay) for LLM pretraining (5.2).
Typically train on a much larger dataset for one epoch rather than many epochs on a tiny one (5.2).
Combine temperature scaling with top-k sampling to trade diversity against coherence; temperature 0 means greedy (5.3).
Save both model and optimizer state_dict if you plan to continue pretraining (5.4).
Load pretrained GPT-2 weights with matching config (1024 context, qkv bias) and check shapes in an assign helper (5.5).
Batch sizes of 1,024 or larger are not uncommon in practice (5.1.3).

terms.definition: measures the difference between two probability distributions; for LLMs, the negative average log probability of the target tokens
exp(loss); the effective vocabulary size about which the model is uncertain at each step
selecting the token with the highest probability score at each step (argmax)
dividing the logits by a number greater than 0 before softmax
restrict sampling to the k most likely tokens by setting other logits to -inf
a variant of Adam that improves the weight decay approach
reusing the token embedding weights in the output layer to reduce parameter count
